title: Kitchen sink
description: Plain JSON Schema plus the `nullable` shorthand. Not a real Actor schema — every property exists to pin one compiler behaviour, and the `description` says which. Property names are the index; nothing here is decorative.

aString.title: A string
aString.description: Scalar, plus keywords with no type meaning: they must all be ignored in silence.

anInteger.description: `integer` collapses to `number` — TypeScript has no integer type.

aNull.description: `null` is a type of its own, not an absence.

multiType.description: A `type` array becomes a union, in declared order.

repeatedType.description: Repeats collapse: `string | number`, not `string | string | number`.

notNullableString.description: `nullable: false` is a no-op, not a null.

alreadyNullable.description: `nullable` on a type that already admits null appends nothing.

nullableArrayOfObjects.description: `nullable` applies to the array, not to its items.

stringEnum.description: An enum becomes a literal union; `enumTitles` is display-only.

mixedEnum.description: Strings, numbers, booleans and null mix freely in one union.

singleMemberEnum.description: One member is a literal, not a one-member union.

repeatedEnumMembers.description: Duplicate members collapse, the same as duplicate types do.

enumOverridesType.description: `enum` fully determines the type, so it wins over a conflicting `type`.

nullableEnum.description: GAP: `nullable` is silently dropped next to an `enum`, with no diagnostic. Expected `"a" | "b" | null`, emitted `"a" | "b"`.

constString.description: GAP: `const` is silently ignored, so the literal widens to `string`.

arrayOfUnions.description: `Array<T>` always, so a union element never needs parenthesizing.

openObject.description: No `additionalProperties`: the writer may add keys, the reader may not read them.

closedObject.description: `additionalProperties: false` closes the object for both variants.

explicitlyOpenObject.description: `additionalProperties: true` says what silence already said.

emptyAdditionalProperties.description: `additionalProperties: {}` types nothing, so it is just open.

objectWithTypedExtras.description: Declared properties and typed extras: a literal intersected with a `Record`.

propertylessObject.description: Never a bare `{}` — in TypeScript that admits `5`.

closedPropertylessObject.description: Closed and empty: `Record<string, never>` accepts no key at all.

deeplyNested.description: Objects, arrays and objects again — indentation has to survive the round trip.

requiredWithDefault.description: Required and defaulted: present for both variants.

optionalWithDefault.description: The platform materializes the default, so the reader always has it and the writer never needs it.

optionalWithoutDefault.description: Optional for both variants, and `| undefined` under exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

optionalUnknown.description: Two things at once: `nullable` with no `type` and no sibling keyword has nothing to widen, so it is dropped; and the resulting `unknown` already admits undefined, so it is not widened with `| undefined` either.

emptySchema.description: `{}` is faithfully `unknown` — a notice, not a degradation.

with-dash.description: Not a bare identifier, so the key is quoted.

2fa.description: Leading digit, so the key is quoted.

class.description: A reserved word is a legal property name, so it stays bare.

$dollar_and_underscore.description: Legal identifier characters that only look like they need quoting.

properties.description: The empty key is legal JSON Schema, and quoting it is the only way to emit it.

refToDefs.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `$ref`. The definition is spelled out right here in `$defs` and we still hand back `unknown`.

refWithSiblings.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `$ref` wins over sibling keywords — the whole node degrades, `type` and `properties` included.

arrayOfRefs.description: NOT SUPPORTED: the warning lands on the items, and the array around it survives as `Array<unknown>`.

oneOfBranch.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `oneOf` — an exclusive union we could express and do not.

anyOfBranch.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `anyOf` — a plain union we could express and do not.

allOfBranch.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `allOf` — an intersection we could express and do not.

notBranch.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `not` has no TypeScript equivalent at all.

conditional.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `if` / `then` / `else` — one warning naming all three.

patternKeys.description: NOT SUPPORTED: `patternProperties` — a template literal key type we could express and do not.

tupleItems.description: NOT SUPPORTED: positional `items`. A tuple is still an array, so `Array<unknown>` is a sound degradation.

objectEnum.description: NOT SUPPORTED: an `enum` of objects cannot be written as a literal.

arrayEnum.description: NOT SUPPORTED: an `enum` of arrays, same reason.

escaped/key~with~specials.description: NOT SUPPORTED, and the point is the JSON Pointer: `/` and `~` must be escaped per RFC 6901 so the path is machine-usable.

prefixItemsTuple.description: GAP: `prefixItems` is the 2020-12 tuple syntax and we do not even know to warn — silently `Array<unknown>`.

unevaluatedExtras.description: GAP: `unevaluatedProperties` is silently ignored, so the object stays open.

constrainedKeys.description: GAP: `propertyNames` is silently ignored, so the key type stays `string`.

containsANumber.description: GAP: `contains` is silently ignored — no items, so `Array<unknown>`.

dependentKeys.description: GAP: `dependentRequired` / `dependentSchemas` are silently ignored, so conditional requiredness is lost.

readOnlyValue.description: GAP: `readOnly` is silently ignored — the emitted property is not `readonly`.

deprecatedValue.description: GAP: `deprecated` is silently ignored — no `@deprecated` reaches the output.

address.description: Reachable only through `$ref`, so nothing here is ever read. `$defs` itself is not warned about — without a `$ref` it is dead weight, and with one the `$ref` is the warning.
